a.summary: The hoisted body is the pre-0d68f02 loop (`recordNumSignatures(numSigners); for (var signer : signers) sign(signer);`), which writes signatures one at a time as it iterates. Main rewrote it to pre-resolve every signer's slot first, so an unknown signer or a duplicate is rejected before ANY byte is written; that is the whole point of commit 0d68f02 / 91bc814's "preserve signer state after failures". With v1_tx's body, `sign(List.of(feePayer, unknownSigner))` writes the fee payer's real signature and only then throws, leaving a half-signed transaction, and `sign(List.of(feePayer, feePayer))` writes slot 0 twice and reports success while slot 1 stays zeroed. Main's test `TransactionSigningTests.collectionSigningIsOrderIndependentAndPrevalidatesTheAssignment` asserts both rejected cases leave BOTH signature slots all-zero, and `signCollectionRejectsWrongSignerCount` asserts the same for a count mismatch. NOTE: this fix depends on the private `signerIndex(Signer)` helper introduced by the first concern above — apply that one first.

b.summary: VERIFIED (find-string confirmed unique). The hoisted body is the pre-0d68f02 loop (`recordNumSignatures(numSigners); for (var signer : signers) sign(signer);`), which writes signatures one at a time as it iterates. Main rewrote it to pre-resolve every signer's slot first so an unknown signer or a duplicate is rejected before ANY byte is written — the point of "preserve signer state after failures". With v1_tx's body, `sign(List.of(feePayer, unknownSigner))` writes the fee payer's real signature and only then throws, and `sign(List.of(feePayer, feePayer))` writes slot 0 twice and reports success while slot 1 stays zeroed. I read main's `collectionSigningIsOrderIndependentAndPrevalidatesTheAssignment`: it asserts reverse-order collection signing produces bytes identical to sequential `sign(feePayer); sign(authority)` (which the replacement satisfies because both paths write the required-signer count and then per-slot signatures), and asserts that both the unknown-signer and duplicate-signer calls leave BOTH 64-byte slots all-zero; `signCollectionRejectsWrongSignerCount` asserts the same for a count mismatch, including for the SequencedCollection overload. Depends on the private `signerIndex(Signer)` helper from the first concern — apply that one first. The `seenSignerIndexes` array is safe at size `passedSigners` because the count check has already established `passedSigners == numSigners()` and `signerIndex` only returns values below `numSigners()`.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.
